facts.fact_text: One of the unauthorised demonstrations in Baku took place on 19 June 2010.
One of the unauthorised demonstrations in Baku took place on 2 April 2011.
The applicants decided to participate in the demonstration of 2 April 2011.

Video recordings submitted by some applicants show that on 2 April 2011, as soon as protesters began gathering in central streets of Baku, marching and chanting slogans calling for the government's resignation, the police started to disperse the demonstration.
The applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 were arrested during the dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011.
The applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 were brought to various police offices for questioning as witnesses following their arrest on 2 April 2011.
Later on 2 April 2011, formal decisions were drawn up to detain the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 as suspects in criminal cases.

On 4 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation of or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).

The administrative-offence report stated that the applicant in application no. 56317/11 had committed an administrative offence under Article 310.1 (failure to comply with a lawful order of a police officer) of the Code of Administrative Offences.
By a letter of 31 March 2011, the Baku City Executive Authority refused to authorise the holding of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 at the place indicated by the organisers.
The Baku City Executive Authority proposed by its letter of 31 March 2011 that the demonstration of 2 April 2011 be held at a different location from the one indicated by the organisers.

The organisers of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 decided to hold the demonstration in the central squares of Baku despite the Baku City Executive Authority's refusal to authorise the originally proposed location.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 stated that if there was an attempt to hold a public assembly in places not agreed upon with the Baku City Executive Authority, illegal actions consisting of breach of public order and insubordination to lawful demands of public officers, or causing inconvenience to the population, or causing disruption of the normal functioning of transport, enterprises, bodies and organisations, would be prevented in accordance with the law.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 stated that prescribed relevant measures would be taken against the applicant in application no. 59661/12 and the other addressees as organisers of the public assemblies if they attempted to hold a public assembly in places not agreed upon with the Baku City Executive Authority.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 contained a warning that the mentioned actions entailed criminal responsibility under Article 220 (mass disorder) of the Criminal Code.

The notice issued by the Baku city prosecutor's office on 1 April 2011 contained a warning that the mentioned actions entailed criminal responsibility under Article 233 (organisation or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order) of the Criminal Code.
The dispersal of the demonstration of 2 April 2011 resulted in isolated incidents of clashes between police officers and demonstrators.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 inflicted physical injuries on around twenty-five police officers.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 damaged two private vehicles.
It appears that several demonstrators at the demonstration of 2 April 2011 broke windows of some shops and offices located near the place where the demonstration was held.

On 4 April 2011 the prosecution formally charged the applicants in applications nos. 56317/11, 67932/11, 27472/12 and 59661/12 with a criminal offence under Article 233 of the Criminal Code (organisation of or active participation in actions causing a breach of public order).
According to the applicant Mr Tural Abbasli (application no. 27472/12), on 2 April 2011 he was subjected to ill-treatment during his arrest.
According to the applicant Mr Tural Abbasli (application no. 27472/12), on 2 April 2011 he was subjected to ill-treatment while in police custody.
On 4 April 2011 Mr Tural Abbasli (applicant in application no. 27472/12) complained of his ill-treatment to a judge deciding on his pre-trial detention.
The judge to whom Mr Tural Abbasli complained of ill-treatment on 4 April 2011 sent the complaint to the Baku city prosecutor's office for examination.

On 25 April 2011 the Baku city prosecutor's office refused to institute criminal proceedings in connection with Mr Tural Abbasli's (applicant in application no. 27472/12) allegations of ill-treatment.

Mr Tural Abbasli (applicant in application no. 27472/12) lodged a complaint with the Sabail District Court in respect of the Baku city prosecutor's office's decision of 25 April 2011 refusing to institute criminal proceedings regarding his allegations of ill-treatment.
On 8 September 2011 the Sabail District Court dismissed Mr Tural Abbasli's (applicant in application no. 27472/12) complaint against the Baku city prosecutor's office's decision of 25 April 2011.
